text: Paper overview: George B. Field (1965) → Exhibit 03 / Field 1965 / Figure 1 A map of growing modes. The stability domains place condensation and acoustic growth in a common plane. Two straight neutral lines count growing roots; two hatched regions distinguish oscillation from non-oscillatory evolution. Equation-based reconstruction, numerically validated. The presentation is modernized; there is no digitized pointwise comparison with the original printed figure. The domains, recomputed. Field (1965), Figure 1, printed p. 536; γ = 5/3. Color indicates the number of roots with positive real part, counted with multiplicity. Hatching means three real distinct roots. Neutral lines are treated separately. The circular annotation guide in the original is omitted because it is not a stability boundary. SVG figurePNG figureDomain grid / CSVConductive paths / CSVValidation / JSON Read the axes Conduction is already on the horizontal axis. Equation (17) defines y = n/(kc), σρ = kρ/k, and σT′ = kT/k + k/kK. The horizontal coordinate includes the positive thermal-conduction contribution. Both coordinates and y are dimensionless; c is the adiabatic sound speed. y³ + σT′y² + y + (σT′ − σρ)/γ = 0 Equation (18). This normalization uses kc; Figures 2 and 3 instead use kρc. Two different boundaries Growth and oscillation answer different questions. The neutral lines The solid line σρ = σT′ has a zero root and is the isobaric neutral line. The dashed line σρ = −(γ − 1)σT′ has purely imaginary roots and is the isentropic neutral line. The hatched thorns The discriminant boundary changes the character of the roots. Inside the hatching, all three roots are real and distinct. Outside, there is one real root and a complex conjugate pair. The hatching is not an additional instability threshold. A growing root means Re(y) > 0. A complex conjugate pair with positive real part counts as two growing roots. Away from neutral lines, the count is: N = 1[σρ > σT′] + 2[σρ < −(γ − 1)σT′] Here 1[condition] is 1 when the condition is true, otherwise 0. On neutral lines the CSV leaves N blank, so zero-real-part roots are not classified by an off-boundary rule. The discriminant Keep Field’s sign convention. Write t = σT′ and r = σρ. Field’s equation (19) defines: D = [(t − r)/γ − t/3 + 2t³/27]²/4 + [1 − t²/3]³/27 For this definition, D < 0 gives three real roots, while D > 0 gives a complex pair. The conventional cubic discriminant is −108D, with the opposite sign. Equation (20) supplies the thorn boundaries; their tips are triple roots at t = ±√3, r = (1 − γ/9)t. One theory, three views Follow a path into Figures 2 and 3. With q = k/kρ > 0, equation (28) gives r = 1/q and t = α/q + βq = αr + β/r. The green paths use α = 1/2, as in Figure 2; the brown paths use α = −2, as in Figure 3. Each family has β = 0.01, 0.1, 1, with dotted zero-conduction reference rays. Increasing wavenumber moves toward smaller positive r. Conduction shifts the path to the right, where it can cross the neutral lines. The growth-rate normalization converts as x = qy. The validation checks this mapping using all three roots along each conducting path. A path can cross the wave neutral line while condensation is still unstable. The map counts all growing roots; the wave cutoff in Figure 3 concerns only the acoustic pair. Reproduce it Build the map from its equations. Save these three files together. The recorded environment uses Python 3.9.6, NumPy 2.0.2, and Matplotlib 3.9.4. No source PDF, external data, or local helper module is needed after installing dependencies. reproduce-map.pyconfig-map.jsonrequirements.txtTechnical notesFull dependency versions python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt .venv/bin/python reproduce-map.py --output output Validation and limits Check the roots behind every region. Compare analytical root counts and D-based topology with numerical roots on an independent grid, away from boundaries. Compare the full root set with eigenvalues of independently assembled linearized fluid equations. Check polynomial residuals, D = 0 on the thorn curves, and the triple-root conditions at both tips. Check the neutral-line factorizations and the path mapping to Figures 2 and 3. Check conductive-path intersections with the appropriate neutral line. All 15 checks passed. The validation report records the number of grid points tested, measured errors, tolerances, environment, and code hashes. The plotted grid has 161 × 161 points; numerical root checks use a separate grid. The graph is reconstructed from the published equations, with modernized coloring, labels, and a legend. No quantitative error relative to digitized original boundaries is claimed. Repeated-root topology labels in the CSV use an absolute D tolerance of 10⁻¹⁰; neutral-line counts are blank. Source and related exhibits. George B. Field (1965), Thermal Instability, The Astrophysical Journal 142, 531–567. Figure 1; equations (17)–(28).
